# Does Medicare Cover Cataract Surgery? | Dr. Robert Weinstock, Largo FL

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/does-medicare-cover-cataract-surgery/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Insurance

# What Medicare Covers for Cataract Surgery

Medicare covers medically necessary cataract surgery, but not every lens or upgrade. Here's what's included, what you may pay, and the questions to ask before surgery.

**By[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · Largo, FL

**Published** November 17, 2026**Medically reviewed** November 17, 20266 min read

**On this page**

  1. What Medicare covers
  2. What you may pay
  3. Premium lenses and upgrades
  4. If you have Medicare Advantage
  5. Glasses after cataract surgery
  6. Questions to ask before surgery
  7. FAQ
  8. Sources

**Key takeaways**

  * Medicare Part B may cover cataract surgery that implants a conventional intraocular lens.
  * After the Part B deductible, you generally pay 20% of the Medicare-approved amount; a Medigap policy can help with that share.
  * Premium lenses that also correct astigmatism or near vision cost extra, and Medicare must always let you choose a standard lens.
  * After each covered cataract surgery with a lens implant, Part B covers one pair of standard eyeglasses or one set of contacts.

## What Medicare covers

Medicare Part B (Medical Insurance) may cover cataract surgery that implants a conventional intraocular lens.1 Coverage applies when your doctor determines surgery is medically necessary, typically because the cataract is affecting your daily life.2

Cataract surgery removes the cloudy natural lens and, in most cases, replaces it with a clear artificial lens.1

## What you may pay

For Original Medicare, after you meet the Part B deductible, you generally pay 20% of the Medicare-approved amount.2 If you have a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) policy, it can cover all or part of that 20% coinsurance.3

Costs vary by where surgery is performed. Medicare's online [procedure price lookup](https://www.medicare.gov/procedure-price-lookup/) can give you an estimate, and our team will walk you through your own numbers before surgery.

Questions about your own eyes?

Book a consultation with Dr. Weinstock in Largo.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## Premium lenses and upgrades

Medicare pays for what it takes to restore functional vision, which is surgery with a conventional lens. If you choose a lens that also corrects astigmatism or reduces your need for reading glasses, you can pay the difference for the premium portion.4

Compare [premium lens implant options](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/premium-lens-implants/). Two protections are worth knowing. Medicare patients must always be able to choose the standard lens, and a surgeon cannot require a premium lens as a condition of surgery.4

"A premium lens is a choice, never a requirement. We show patients exactly what each option does and what it costs, in writing, before anything is scheduled."

DR. ROBERT J. WEINSTOCK · CATARACT & REFRACTIVE SURGEON

## If you have Medicare Advantage

Medicare Advantage plans must provide at least the same coverage as Original Medicare, which includes cataract surgery with a standard lens.5 Some plans add vision benefits. Advantage plans may require precertification before a practice can bill you for a premium lens upgrade, so we check with your plan in advance.6

## Glasses after cataract surgery

Medicare usually does not cover eyeglasses or contact lenses. The exception: after each cataract surgery that implants an intraocular lens, Part B covers one pair of eyeglasses with standard frames or one set of contact lenses.2 They must come from a supplier enrolled in Medicare.5

## Questions to ask before surgery

  * Is my surgery considered medically necessary, and is my lens choice covered?
  * What will I pay for the surgeon, the surgery center and any lens upgrade?
  * Does my Medicare Advantage plan require approval before surgery?
  * Which lens fits my eyes and lifestyle, and what does each option do differently?

Not sure you need surgery yet? Start with [the 7 signs it may be time for cataract surgery](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/signs-you-need-cataract-surgery/).

## Frequently asked questions

Does Medicare cover laser cataract surgery?

Medicare covers medically necessary cataract surgery. Some laser steps used for extra refractive benefits, such as correcting astigmatism, can carry an added cost. Ask for a written quote before surgery.

Does Medicare pay for both eyes?

Medicare covers cataract surgery for each eye when surgery is medically necessary for that eye. Most patients have the eyes done on separate days.

Will Medicare pay for my glasses after surgery?

After each cataract surgery that implants a lens, Part B covers one pair of eyeglasses with standard frames or one set of contacts from a Medicare-enrolled supplier.

Can I choose a premium lens with Medicare?

Yes. You can choose a premium lens and pay the difference for the premium portion, but you can always choose the standard lens that Medicare covers.

## Sources

  2. FedRateCalc. Does Medicare cover cataract surgery? (quoting Medicare.gov coverage pages). <https://fedratecalc.com/does-medicare-cover-cataract-surgery/>
  3. AARP. Does Medicare cover cataract surgery? <https://www.aarp.org/medicare/faq/does-medicare-cover-cataract-surgery/>

# LASIK vs. EVO ICL: Which Is Right for You? | Dr. Robert Weinstock, Largo FL

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/lasik-vs-evo-icl/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Vision Correction

# LASIK vs. EVO ICL: How to Know Which Fits You

Both can free you from glasses and contacts, but they work in very different ways. Here's how to tell which one fits your eyes, your prescription and your life.

**By[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · Largo, FL

**Published** November 17, 2026**Medically reviewed** November 17, 20267 min read

**On this page**

  1. How each procedure works
  2. LASIK and EVO ICL side by side
  3. Who tends to fit LASIK
  4. Who tends to fit EVO ICL
  5. What if you're over 45?
  6. Questions to ask your surgeon
  7. FAQ
  8. Sources

**Key takeaways**

  * LASIK uses a laser to reshape the cornea and is FDA approved to treat nearsightedness, farsightedness and astigmatism.
  * EVO ICL is a thin lens placed inside the eye, behind the iris, without removing corneal tissue.
  * EVO ICL is often considered for higher prescriptions, thinner corneas or dry eye concerns.
  * Neither procedure prevents the need for reading glasses as you age; lens-based options may fit better after about 45.

## How each procedure works

**LASIK** uses a laser to reshape the cornea, the clear front window of the eye, so light focuses correctly. LASIK has been approved by the FDA to treat nearsightedness, farsightedness and astigmatism.1

**EVO ICL** (Implantable Collamer Lens) is a thin lens placed inside the eye, behind the iris, in front of your natural lens. Unlike LASIK, it corrects vision without removing corneal tissue.2 Because your natural lens stays in place, the approach is described as reversible and keeps future treatment options open.3

The FDA approved the EVO ICL in the United States on March 25, 2022, for correcting nearsightedness and nearsightedness with astigmatism.4 Earlier versions of the lens required a small laser opening in the iris before surgery; the EVO design does not.5

## LASIK and EVO ICL side by side

| LASIK| EVO ICL  
---|---|---  
How it works| Laser reshapes the cornea| Thin lens placed behind the iris  
Corneal tissue removed| Yes| No  
Reversible| No| The lens can be removed  
Often a good fit for| Stable prescriptions and healthy corneas| Higher prescriptions, thinner corneas or dry eye concerns  
Treats reading vision with age| No| No  
  
The right choice depends on measurements only a full exam can provide, including your prescription, corneal thickness and shape, and the space inside your eye. Learn more about [LASIK in Largo](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/lasik/) and [EVO ICL in Largo](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/evo-icl/).

Questions about your own eyes?

Book a consultation with Dr. Weinstock in Largo.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## Who tends to fit LASIK

LASIK is often a strong option for adults whose prescription has been stable and whose corneas are healthy and thick enough to reshape. A thorough baseline evaluation decides whether you are a good candidate.6

Dry eye matters. The FDA notes that existing dry eye can get worse after LASIK, and some people develop dry eye as a result of surgery, so you should be screened before treatment.7

## Who tends to fit EVO ICL

EVO ICL is often considered when LASIK is not the best fit: higher amounts of nearsightedness, corneas that are thin or irregular, or dry eye that makes corneal surgery less appealing. At FDA approval it was indicated for adults 21 to 45,8 and the FDA has since approved an expanded age indication.3

"Patients often come in asking for LASIK by name. My job is to measure their eyes and tell them honestly which procedure will give them the best long-term result."

DR. ROBERT J. WEINSTOCK · CATARACT & REFRACTIVE SURGEON

## What if you're over 45?

Around your mid-40s, the eye's natural lens starts losing its ability to focus up close, a condition called presbyopia. Neither LASIK nor ICL stops that, and the FDA notes that people who used reading glasses before LASIK may still need them afterward.7

For many people in this stage, a lens-based procedure such as Clear Lens Exchange can address near and distance vision together and remove the chance of a future cataract. See [Clear Lens Exchange in Largo](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/clear-lens-exchange/).

## Questions to ask your surgeon

  * Which procedure do my measurements support, and why?
  * How many of these procedures have you performed with this laser or lens?7
  * Will I still need reading glasses, now or later?
  * What does recovery look like, and how many follow-up visits will I have?

After LASIK, expect to see your doctor within the first 24 to 48 hours and at regular visits after that.6

## Frequently asked questions

Is EVO ICL better than LASIK?

Neither is better for everyone. LASIK is a strong option for many people with stable prescriptions and healthy corneas, while EVO ICL is often a better fit for higher prescriptions, thin corneas or dry eye concerns.

Can EVO ICL be removed?

Yes. Because the lens is placed inside the eye without removing corneal tissue, it can be removed or exchanged if needed.

Will I need reading glasses after LASIK or ICL?

Possibly. Both procedures correct distance vision but do not stop presbyopia, the age-related loss of near focus that usually begins in the mid-40s.

How do I know which one I qualify for?

A full evaluation measures your prescription, corneal thickness and shape, and the internal dimensions of your eye. Those measurements determine which procedure is safe and effective for you.

  3. Eyes On Eyecare Glance. FDA approves expanded age indication for STAAR's EVO/EVO+ Visian ICLs. February 19, 2026. <https://glance.eyesoneyecare.com/stories/2026-02-19/fda-approves-expanded-age-indication-for-staar-s-evo-evo-visian-icls/>
  4. Healio. FDA approves EVO Visian lens. April 12, 2022. <https://www.healio.com/news/ophthalmology/20220412/fda-approves-evo-visian-lens>

# 7 Signs You May Need Cataract Surgery | Dr. Robert Weinstock, Largo FL

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/signs-you-need-cataract-surgery/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Cataracts

# 7 Signs It May Be Time for Cataract Surgery

Cataracts creep in slowly, so most people adapt without noticing. Here are the seven signs a cataract may be affecting your life, and how to know when surgery makes sense.

**By[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · Largo, FL

**Published** November 17, 2026**Medically reviewed** November 17, 20266 min read

**On this page**

  1. What is a cataract?
  2. The 7 signs to watch for
  3. When is it time for surgery?
  4. What cataract surgery involves
  5. FAQ
  6. Sources

**Key takeaways**

  * A cataract is a clouding of the eye's natural lens, and it usually develops slowly.
  * Common signs include blurry or dim vision, glare and halos, poor night vision and faded colors.
  * Surgery is usually the right time when blurry vision gets in the way of everyday life.
  * Cataract surgery replaces the cloudy lens with a clear artificial lens, and the right lens can also reduce your need for glasses.

## What is a cataract?

A cataract is a clouding of the lens inside your eye, which is normally clear.1 The lens sits behind the colored part of your eye and focuses light, so as it clouds, the image you see turns blurry, dim and washed out.

Age is the biggest risk factor. By age 80, more than half of all Americans either have a cataract or have had cataract surgery.2 Diabetes, long-term steroid use, eye injuries, previous eye surgery and years of sun exposure can all speed things up.1

## The 7 signs to watch for

Because cataracts usually grow slowly, early changes are easy to miss.3 These are the signs eye surgeons hear about most often:

### 1\. Cloudy, blurry or dim vision

It can feel like looking through a smudged or foggy window, even with clean glasses.3

### 2\. Glare and halos around lights

Headlights, lamps or sunlight may seem too bright, or you may see rings around lights.2

### 3\. Trouble seeing at night

Night driving is often the first thing people start avoiding.2

### 4\. Colors that look faded or yellowed

Whites can look dingy and blues can look dull, a change many patients only notice after surgery.3

### 5\. Frequent prescription changes

If your glasses or contacts never seem quite right for long, a changing lens may be the reason.3

### 6\. Double vision in one eye

Seeing a ghost image with one eye closed can be a sign of a cataract.3

### 7\. Needing more light to read

If you keep turning up the lamp or reaching for a flashlight to read menus, the lens may be letting in less light.4

**See a doctor right away** if you notice a sudden shower of floaters, flashes of light or a curtain over part of your vision. Those are usually not cataract symptoms and can signal a retinal emergency.

Questions about your own eyes?

Book a consultation with Dr. Weinstock in Largo.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## When is it time for surgery?

There is rarely a rush. In general, cataract surgery makes sense when blurry vision starts to get in the way of everyday life, like driving, reading, working or enjoying hobbies.1

A comprehensive eye exam is the only way to confirm a cataract and rule out other conditions that cause similar symptoms.1

"The question I ask patients is simple: what are you no longer doing because of your eyes? That answer usually tells us when the time is right."

DR. ROBERT J. WEINSTOCK · CATARACT & REFRACTIVE SURGEON

## What cataract surgery involves

Cataract surgery removes the cloudy natural lens and, in most cases, replaces it with a clear artificial lens called an intraocular lens (IOL).5 It is an outpatient procedure.

Today's lens options can do more than restore clarity. With the right lens, cataract surgery can also correct nearsightedness, farsightedness or astigmatism, which means less dependence on glasses afterward. Dr. Weinstock has served as a principal investigator on dozens of clinical studies of new intraocular lenses and surgical systems, so lens selection is a big part of every consultation. Learn more about [laser cataract surgery in Largo](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/laser-cataract-surgery/) and [premium lens implants](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/premium-lens-implants/).

Wondering what it costs? Read [what Medicare covers for cataract surgery](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/does-medicare-cover-cataract-surgery/).

## Frequently asked questions

Can cataracts go away on their own?

No. A cataract does not clear up on its own. Brighter lighting and updated glasses can help for a while, but surgery is the only way to remove a cataract.

Is there harm in waiting?

For most people, waiting is safe as long as vision is not interfering with daily life or safety, such as driving. Your eye surgeon can tell you whether waiting makes sense for your eyes.

Does cataract surgery hurt?

Cataract surgery is performed with numbing drops, and most patients describe feeling pressure rather than pain.

Can I get rid of my glasses after cataract surgery?

Many patients can reduce their need for glasses by choosing a lens that also corrects nearsightedness, farsightedness or astigmatism. Your consultation will cover which lenses fit your eyes and lifestyle.

About Dr. Weinstock

## A surgeon who helps shape _the field he practices  in_

Robert J. Weinstock, MD, is a board-certified ophthalmologist who specializes in cataract and refractive surgery, including laser cataract surgery, premium and light adjustable lens implants, LASIK, EVO ICL and refractive lens exchange. He practices at The Eye Institute of West Florida in Largo and Clearwater, where he is Medical Director, and serves as Regional Medical Director for EyeCare Partners.

He trained in cataract and refractive surgery under his father, Stephen M. Weinstock, MD, completing his fellowship at The Eye Institute of West Florida in 2002. Since then he has served as principal investigator on 32 clinical studies of new lenses, lasers and surgical systems, written 14 textbook chapters, and lectured at major meetings including ASCRS, the American Academy of Ophthalmology and AECOS.

He has written textbook chapters on microincisional and 3D heads-up digital cataract surgery, helped develop TrueVision 3D surgical visualization, and teaches the next generation as Fellowship Director at The Eye Institute of West Florida and Ophthalmology Rotation Director for Evara Health residents.

He has written more than 200 published articles and given more than 500 lectures internationally. Outside the operating room, he lives in Tampa Bay with his wife and three sons, and spends his free time fishing, freediving, spearfishing and snowboarding.

Nationally

### Top 1% in cataract surgery volume

Ranks in the top 1 percent of cataract surgeons nationally by surgical volume.

Career

### 50,000+ cataract surgeries

More than 50,000 cataract surgeries and more than 100,000 laser and ophthalmic procedures.

Since 2008

### First in the world: heads-up 3D digital eye surgery

The first surgeon in the world to perform heads-up 3D digital eye surgery, and the first to report it for cataract surgery in the medical literature. He helped TrueVision develop the technology.

[Source](https://eyewiki.org/Three-Dimensional_Display_Systems_for_Surgery_in_Ophthalmology)Laser cataract

### One of the first in the world

One of the first surgeons in the world to perform laser cataract surgery, and the first to perform commercial cases with the LENSAR ALLY adaptive laser system in 2022.

[Source](https://www.massdevice.com/lensar-announces-first-patients-treated-with-ally-adaptive-cataract-treatment/)Implants & lasers

### Pioneer of modern lens technology

Pioneered microincisional cataract instrumentation, accommodating and presbyopia-correcting implants, intraoperative aberrometry, minimally invasive glaucoma surgery, laser astigmatism correction, toric implants and light adjustable lenses.

[Source](https://www.healio.com/news/ophthalmology/20250401/a-surgeons-guide-to-undergoing-refractive-lens-exchange)Complex cases

### Pioneer in complex implant surgery

A pioneer in complex implant surgery, including sutured IOLs, IOL exchanges and traumatic cataracts.

[Source](https://crstoday.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2024/03/0324CRST_editorial.pdf)

## About _Dr.  Weinstock_

Is Dr. Robert Weinstock board certified?

Yes. Dr. Weinstock has been a Diplomate of the American Board of Ophthalmology since 2003. He also holds American Board of Eye Surgery sub-specialty certifications in refractive surgery (LASIK) and cataract and implant surgery, both earned in 2007.

Where did Dr. Weinstock train?

He earned his MD at The Chicago Medical School, completed his ophthalmology residency at Saint Louis University School of Medicine, where he served as Clinical and Administrative Chief Resident, and completed a fellowship in cataract and refractive surgery at The Eye Institute of West Florida.

Where does Dr. Weinstock see patients?

Dr. Weinstock sees patients at The Eye Institute of West Florida in Largo, with an additional office in Clearwater. He performs surgery at the Largo Ambulatory Surgery Center, where he is Medical Director.

What procedures does Dr. Weinstock specialize in?

He specializes in cataract and refractive surgery, including laser cataract surgery, premium and light adjustable lens implants, LASIK, EVO ICL and refractive lens exchange.

Is Dr. Weinstock involved in research and teaching?

Yes. He has served on 42 clinical studies, 32 of them as principal investigator, written 14 textbook chapters and is an Assistant Clinical Professor of Ophthalmology at the University of South Florida Eye Institute.

## Answers _before you  visit_

How do I know if I need cataract surgery?

Common signs include cloudy or dim vision, glare and halos around lights, faded colors and trouble driving at night. A comprehensive eye exam with Dr. Weinstock is the only way to know for sure.

Am I a candidate for LASIK?

Good LASIK candidates are adults with a stable prescription and healthy corneas. If your corneas are thin or your prescription is high, EVO ICL or Clear Lens Exchange may be a better fit. Your consultation will tell you which.

Does Medicare cover cataract surgery?

Medicare and most insurance plans typically cover medically necessary cataract surgery. Our team reviews your coverage, and any cost for premium lens options, before your procedure.

Where is Weinstock Vision located?

Our main office is at 1225 West Bay Drive in Largo, Florida, and we serve patients from Clearwater, St. Petersburg and Tampa. Surgery is performed at the Largo Ambulatory Surgery Center, where Dr. Weinstock is Medical Director.

What are your office hours?

We are open Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, and closed Saturday and Sunday.

Who will perform my surgery?

Dr. Robert J. Weinstock, a board-certified, fellowship-trained cataract and refractive surgeon named one of Newsweek's America's Best Eye Doctors.

# Clear Lens Exchange in Largo, FL | Dr. Robert Weinstock

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/clear-lens-exchange/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Procedures · Largo, Florida

# Clear Lens Exchange in Largo, Florida

Replace your natural lens to correct near and far vision, and never develop a cataract.

**Performed by[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · 100,000+ procedures

**On this page**

  1. How Clear Lens Exchange works
  2. Who is a good candidate
  3. Cost
  4. FAQ

Clear Lens Exchange, also called refractive lens exchange, replaces the eye's natural lens with an artificial lens before a cataract forms, to correct your prescription and reduce the need for glasses. It is usually for adults over about 45 who need help with both distance and reading vision, or who are not good candidates for LASIK. Because the natural lens is replaced, a cataract can never develop.

**Who it suits** Adults over about 45, or high prescriptions

**Treats** Distance, reading vision and astigmatism

**Bonus** You will never develop a cataract

**Recovery** Similar to cataract surgery

## How Clear Lens Exchange works

The procedure is the same as modern cataract surgery: the natural lens is removed through a tiny opening and replaced with an intraocular lens chosen for your eyes. With a [premium lens](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/premium-lens-implants/), many people reduce or eliminate their need for glasses for both near and far.

## Who is a good candidate

Clear Lens Exchange often fits people in their mid-40s and older who are starting to need reading glasses, people with high prescriptions, and people who are not candidates for [LASIK](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/lasik/). Dr. Weinstock had refractive lens exchange himself, with the Light Adjustable Lens.

Find out which option fits your eyes.

Consultations with Dr. Weinstock in Largo and Clearwater.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## Cost

Because Clear Lens Exchange is elective, it is usually not covered by insurance. We provide a written quote before anything is scheduled.

## Clear Lens Exchange FAQ

How is Clear Lens Exchange different from cataract surgery?

The procedure is the same. The difference is timing: Clear Lens Exchange replaces a lens that is still clear, to correct vision rather than to remove a cataract.

Will I need reading glasses after?

With a multifocal, extended-depth-of-focus or Light Adjustable Lens, many people need readers rarely or not at all. Your consultation sets realistic expectations.

Is insurance going to cover it?

Usually not, because it is an elective procedure. You receive a written quote first.

Can I have it if I already had LASIK?

Often yes. Your earlier LASIK is factored into the lens calculations.

How long does the new lens last?

An intraocular lens is designed to last for the rest of your life.

# EVO ICL in Largo, FL | Dr. Robert Weinstock

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/evo-icl/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Procedures · Largo, Florida

# EVO ICL in Largo, Florida

An implantable lens for higher prescriptions or corneas too thin for LASIK.

**Performed by[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · 100,000+ procedures

**On this page**

  1. How EVO ICL works
  2. Who is a good candidate
  3. What to expect
  4. FAQ

EVO ICL (Implantable Collamer Lens) is a thin lens placed inside the eye, behind the iris and in front of your natural lens, to correct nearsightedness with or without astigmatism. Unlike LASIK, it does not remove corneal tissue and can be removed if needed. It is often a strong option for higher prescriptions, thin corneas or dry eye concerns.

**Who it suits** Nearsighted adults, including high prescriptions

**Corneal tissue removed** None

**Reversible** The lens can be removed

**FDA approved** March 2022 in the U.S.

## How EVO ICL works

The lens is folded and placed through a tiny opening, then unfolds behind the iris. Because it adds focusing power rather than reshaping the cornea, it can treat prescriptions that are too high for laser correction. The FDA approved the EVO ICL in the United States in March 2022.

## Who is a good candidate

EVO ICL is often considered for people with moderate to high nearsightedness, corneas that are thin or irregular, or dry eye that makes corneal surgery less appealing. Measurements of the space inside your eye confirm whether the lens will fit.

Comparing options? Read [LASIK vs. EVO ICL](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/lasik-vs-evo-icl/) or learn about [LASIK in Largo](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/lasik/).

Find out which option fits your eyes.

Consultations with Dr. Weinstock in Largo and Clearwater.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## What to expect

  1. **Evaluation.** Precise measurements choose the lens size and power.
  2. **Procedure.** Numbing drops and a short outpatient procedure for each eye.
  3. **Recovery.** Many people see well within a day or two, with follow-up visits to check eye pressure and lens position.

## EVO ICL FAQ

Is EVO ICL better than LASIK?

Neither is better for everyone. EVO ICL is often a better fit for higher prescriptions, thin corneas or dry eye, while LASIK suits many people with moderate prescriptions and healthy corneas.

Can EVO ICL be removed?

Yes. The lens is placed without removing corneal tissue and can be removed or exchanged if needed.

Will I feel the lens?

No. The lens sits inside the eye behind the iris, where it cannot be felt or seen by others.

Does EVO ICL treat astigmatism?

A toric version of the lens corrects nearsightedness with astigmatism.

Will I still need reading glasses later?

EVO ICL corrects distance vision but does not stop presbyopia, so reading glasses may be needed after about age 45.

# Laser Cataract Surgery in Largo, FL | Dr. Robert Weinstock

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/laser-cataract-surgery/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Procedures · Largo, Florida

# Laser Cataract Surgery in Largo, Florida

Remove a cloudy lens with laser precision and correct your prescription in the same procedure.

**Performed by[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · 100,000+ procedures

**On this page**

  1. How laser cataract surgery works
  2. Who is a good candidate
  3. What to expect, step by step
  4. Cost and coverage
  5. FAQ

Laser cataract surgery removes the cloudy natural lens of the eye and replaces it with a clear artificial lens, using a femtosecond laser for key steps that are traditionally done by hand. It is for adults whose cataracts are blurring their vision or making daily tasks like driving and reading harder. Most people see more clearly within days, and the right lens can also reduce the need for glasses.

**Who it suits** Adults with cataracts affecting daily life

**How long** Usually under 30 minutes per eye

**Recovery** Most resume normal activity within days

**Where** Largo, with consultations in Largo and Clearwater

## How laser cataract surgery works

A cataract is a clouding of the lens inside the eye. During surgery, the cloudy lens is removed and replaced with an intraocular lens (IOL). With laser-assisted surgery, a femtosecond laser makes the opening in the lens capsule and softens the cataract so it can be removed gently, with imaging that maps your eye before the laser begins.

Dr. Weinstock performed the first commercial cases with the LENSAR ALLY adaptive laser system in 2022, and has been performing and teaching laser cataract surgery for more than a decade.

## Who is a good candidate

You may be ready for cataract surgery when blurry vision, glare or poor night vision start getting in the way of things you want to do. A full eye exam confirms the cataract and rules out other causes. Not sure yet? Read [the 7 signs it may be time for cataract surgery](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/signs-you-need-cataract-surgery/).

Find out which option fits your eyes.

Consultations with Dr. Weinstock in Largo and Clearwater.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## What to expect, step by step

  1. **Consultation and measurements.** Detailed scans of your eye help choose the lens power and type.
  2. **Choosing your lens.** A standard lens, or a premium lens that can also correct astigmatism or reduce the need for reading glasses.
  3. **Surgery day.** Numbing drops, a brief laser step and lens replacement. You go home the same day with a driver.
  4. **Follow-up.** Checkups the next day and in the weeks after, with eye drops while you heal.

## Cost and coverage

Medicare and most insurance plans cover medically necessary cataract surgery with a standard lens. Premium lens upgrades and some laser steps used to correct astigmatism can carry an added cost, which we explain in writing before anything is scheduled. See [what Medicare covers for cataract surgery](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/does-medicare-cover-cataract-surgery/).

## Laser Cataract Surgery FAQ

Is laser cataract surgery better than traditional cataract surgery?

Both are safe and effective. The laser adds precision to certain steps and can help correct astigmatism at the same time. Dr. Weinstock will recommend the approach that fits your eyes.

Does cataract surgery hurt?

The eye is numbed with drops, and most patients feel only light pressure. You are awake but relaxed, and the procedure is usually brief.

How soon will I see clearly?

Many patients notice clearer vision within a day or two, and vision keeps improving over the following weeks as the eye heals.

Can both eyes be done on the same day?

Most patients have each eye treated on a separate day, usually a week or two apart, so the first eye can heal.

Will I still need glasses?

That depends on the lens you choose. Premium lenses can reduce or remove the need for glasses for many activities.

Where is the surgery performed?

Dr. Weinstock operates in Largo, Florida, and sees patients for consultations in Largo and Clearwater.

# LASIK in Largo, FL | Dr. Robert Weinstock

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/lasik/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Procedures · Largo, Florida

# LASIK in Largo, Florida

Laser vision correction for nearsightedness, farsightedness and astigmatism.

**Performed by[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · 100,000+ procedures

**On this page**

  1. How LASIK works
  2. Who is a good candidate
  3. What to expect
  4. Over 45?
  5. FAQ

LASIK is a laser procedure that reshapes the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye, so light focuses correctly without glasses or contacts. It is FDA approved to treat nearsightedness, farsightedness and astigmatism in adults with a stable prescription and healthy corneas. Most people notice sharper vision within a day.

**Who it suits** Adults with a stable prescription and healthy corneas

**Treats** Nearsightedness, farsightedness, astigmatism

**Recovery** Most see clearly within a day

**Not for** Age-related reading vision changes

## How LASIK works

A laser creates a thin flap in the cornea, a second laser reshapes the tissue beneath it, and the flap is laid back in place. The treatment takes minutes per eye, and you go home the same day.

## Who is a good candidate

Good candidates are adults whose prescription has been stable, with corneas that are healthy and thick enough to treat. A thorough evaluation checks your prescription, corneal thickness and shape, and screens for dry eye, which LASIK can make worse.

If LASIK is not the best fit, an implantable lens such as [EVO ICL](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/evo-icl/) may be. Compare them in [LASIK vs. EVO ICL: how to know which fits you](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/lasik-vs-evo-icl/).

Find out which option fits your eyes.

Consultations with Dr. Weinstock in Largo and Clearwater.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## What to expect

  1. **Evaluation.** Detailed corneal mapping and measurements decide if LASIK is safe for you.
  2. **Treatment.** Numbing drops and a few minutes of laser time per eye.
  3. **Recovery.** Rest the day of surgery, then a checkup within the first 24 to 48 hours.

## Over 45?

LASIK does not stop presbyopia, the age-related loss of reading vision that usually starts in the mid-40s. For many people at that stage, [Clear Lens Exchange](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/clear-lens-exchange/) may be a better fit.

## LASIK FAQ

Is LASIK permanent?

LASIK permanently reshapes the cornea, but the eye can still change with age, including the need for reading glasses after about 45.

Does LASIK hurt?

Numbing drops are used, and most people feel pressure rather than pain. Some mild irritation is common for a few hours afterward.

Can LASIK cause dry eye?

Yes. LASIK can cause or worsen dry eye, which is why you are screened for it before treatment.

How do I know if I qualify?

A full evaluation of your prescription, corneal thickness and shape, and eye health determines whether LASIK is safe and effective for you.

What if I am not a LASIK candidate?

Other options include EVO ICL, an implantable lens that does not remove corneal tissue, and Clear Lens Exchange for people over about 45.

# Premium Lens Implants in Largo, FL | Dr. Robert Weinstock

Source: https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/procedures/premium-lens-implants/
Updated: 2026-11-19

Procedures · Largo, Florida

# Premium Lens Implants in Largo, Florida

Multifocal, toric and light adjustable lenses that can mean less dependence on glasses.

**Performed by[Robert J. Weinstock, MD](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/dr-robert-weinstock/)**Board-certified cataract & refractive surgeon · 100,000+ procedures

**On this page**

  1. Your lens options
  2. How to choose
  3. Cost
  4. FAQ

Premium lens implants are advanced intraocular lenses placed during cataract surgery or lens replacement that do more than restore clear vision. Toric lenses correct astigmatism, multifocal and extended-depth-of-focus lenses help with near and distance vision, and the Light Adjustable Lens can be fine-tuned after surgery. They are for people who want to rely less on glasses after surgery.

**Who it suits** Cataract or lens replacement patients who want fewer glasses

**Options** Toric, multifocal, extended depth of focus, Light Adjustable Lens

**Recovery** Same as cataract surgery

**Coverage** Insurance covers the standard lens; the upgrade is extra

## Your lens options

### Toric lenses

Correct astigmatism, so distance vision can be sharp without glasses.

### Multifocal and extended-depth-of-focus lenses

Provide a range of focus for distance, computer and reading vision, reducing the need for readers.

### Light Adjustable Lens

A lens whose power can be adjusted after surgery with a series of light treatments in the office, so your final vision can be fine-tuned. Dr. Weinstock chose this lens for his own eyes.

## How to choose

The right lens depends on your eye measurements, your eye health and how you spend your day. Someone who reads and drives at night has different needs than a golfer or a pilot. Dr. Weinstock has served as an investigator in dozens of clinical studies of new lenses and surgical systems, and walks every patient through the trade-offs of each option.

Find out which option fits your eyes.

Consultations with Dr. Weinstock in Largo and Clearwater.

[Book a Consultation](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/#contact)

## Cost

Medicare and private insurance pay for cataract surgery with a standard lens. If you choose a premium lens, you pay the difference for the premium portion, and you can always choose the standard lens instead. We give you the costs in writing before surgery. Learn more about [Medicare and premium lenses](https://proposals.localairegistry.com/weinstock/articles/does-medicare-cover-cataract-surgery/).

## Premium Lens Implants FAQ

Which premium lens is best?

There is no single best lens. The right choice depends on your measurements, eye health and lifestyle, which your consultation covers in detail.

Will a premium lens get rid of my glasses completely?

Many patients rarely need glasses after a premium lens, but some still use readers for small print or glasses for night driving. Your surgeon will set honest expectations.

Can I get a premium lens with Medicare?

Yes. Medicare covers the standard lens and surgery, and you pay the difference for the premium portion.

What is the Light Adjustable Lens?

It is an intraocular lens whose power can be adjusted after surgery with light treatments, so your vision can be fine-tuned once your eye has healed.

Do premium lenses cause halos?

Some multifocal lenses can cause halos or glare around lights at night, especially early on. This is one of the trade-offs discussed when choosing a lens.
